question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed opt-in readiness contract, including its public configuration activation boundary and plugin-provider API, before this RFC is accepted?
rationale: The proposed schema and extension boundary create durable operator and plugin compatibility commitments; source-level review cannot determine whether that product direction is desired.

options.title: Accept the readiness direction
options.body: Record approval of the opt-in activation, required/advisory model, subject identity, and activation-scoped provider boundary, then continue implementation review against this RFC.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Approve only the core condition model and defer plugin providers or subject reconciliation until a smaller API proposal is reviewed.

options.title: Decline the direction
options.body: Close or replace the RFC if the existing Gateway checker should remain the only supported readiness contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the readiness direction
recommendation.body: Record approval of the opt-in activation, required/advisory model, subject identity, and activation-scoped provider boundary, then continue implementation review against this RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: giodl73-repo is the available contributor most closely connected to the RFC history and can incorporate the resulting decision record.
